overall: Los Angeles is running warmer than models expected on this overcast, southwest-wind day. The running maximum has already hit 72.0°F as of 15:30 ET — overshooting all three NWP model forecasts (ECMWF 68.4, HRRR 70.4, NBM 67.0) and the NWS narrative high of 70°F. Despite the intraday model flagging a peak around 15:07 ET, residual positive velocity (+1.8°F/hr) and NWP peak-timing consensus pointing to 16–17h ET suggest a bit more warming may still be ahead.
forecast_obs_notes: All NWP models and the official NWS forecast have been beaten by observed reality; the models clustered in the 67–70°F range while the thermometer is already at 72°F. The NWS alerts (Extreme Heat Warning, 108–115°F) are issued by NWS Phoenix for the Arizona desert interior and are not relevant to coastal LA. Model timing spread (ECMWF/HRRR at 16h, NBM at 20h) adds uncertainty about whether the afternoon peak is truly behind us.
max_temp_prediction: With 72.0°F already locked in as the running max and a still-positive warming trend, the final TMAX is most likely to settle in the 74–76°F range. The META (fused) model — the most reliable signal — assigns ~32% to 74–75°F and ~32% to 76–77°F, with 28% to 72–73°F, so roughly two-thirds of probability mass lies above the current running max. The key downside risk is that the peak has effectively passed (intraday timing model) and sea breeze reinforcement under cloudy skies caps further gains; the upside risk is the NWP timing consensus putting the peak ~1.5h ahead. Best single-point estimate is 74.5°F with moderate confidence.
